chunks: A part of the same sermon: Take lesson from useful items of instruction, be cautioned by shining indications, be warned by effective warnings, and benefit from remembrance and preaching.
It is as though the claws of death have clung to you, the ties of hope have been cut from you, terrifying affairs have befallen you, and the march is towards the place where everyone has to go.
(And with every person there is a driver and a witness)
A driver drives her towards her gathering (resurrection); and a witness testifies against her about her deeds.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'driver and witness' in the Quranic verse cited in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs urgent rhetorical devices to shift the audience from passive listening to active spiritual preparation, emphasizing the inevitability of death as a transition rather than an end. This passage reflects the Shia emphasis on *maw'iza* (admonition) as a means to purify the heart, linking the internal witness of deeds with the external reality of the Hereafter. The imagery serves to dismantle worldly attachments (*al-amaniyy*) and instill a sense of immediate accountability before the final gathering.
